shared_elements: bird head with prominent hooked/pointed beak in profile
rows of repeated curved marks reading as feathers or plumage
justification: Both surfaces depict a large raptor-like bird with a hooked beak, an outspread wing rendered as ranked rows of curved feather marks, and clawed feet, which is a reasonably specific shared motif. But A is a single, strictly symmetrical frontal bird filling the whole field, while B is a multi-register composition of several small animals (quadrupeds, snake-like forms, a row of repeated heads under a banded frieze) with the bird only as one profile element among many, so the compositional logic and the accompanying cast of creatures differ substantially.
